segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The weight of leading a whole nation was crushing Moses. He told the LORD he could not carry the people alone, not one more day.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So God told Moses to gather seventy trusted men.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He would take some of the Spirit that rested on Moses and share it with them, and together they would help bear the load.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Spirit came down on those seventy, they began to speak God's words. But two men, Eldad and Medad, had stayed back in the camp — and the Spirit came on them too, right there among the tents.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A runner hurried to Moses with the news.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Joshua, Moses's right-hand man, was worried — stop them, he said. That is not how it is supposed to work.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Enviest thou me for my sake? would God that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the most generous answers in all of scripture. Moses did not guard the gift — he wished it wider.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Moses did not guard the gift — he wished it for everyone. The same Spirit is offered to you. Ask, and receive.
